title: VALORANT Controller Smokes: Timing Around Team Entry
summary: Use Controller abilities to enable teammates rather than placing smokes with no follow-up.
intro: Use Controller abilities to enable teammates rather than placing smokes with no follow-up. This original Digital Racer guide offers practical decisions for players who want better coordination and more predictable results. The examples are deliberately grounded in common teamwork principles, not promises of guaranteed rank gains, exact unverified statistics or secret shortcuts. Test the advice on the current live game, because map layouts and ability behavior can change with updates.

sections.heading: Choose a clear sightline
paragraphs: Before selecting an ability, identify the defender angle it should deny. A smoke that blocks teammates' approach while leaving a strong defender position visible may hurt the attack. Aim to create a deliberate path toward the objective.

sections.heading: Coordinate the entry moment
paragraphs: Tell the Duelist and Initiator when the intended cover will appear. A smoke dropped long before teammates are ready may expire or invite a defender push. Use concise language that indicates the location and planned action.

sections.heading: Respect friendly information
paragraphs: Blocking enemy vision can also prevent your team from seeing a risky corner. Keep an ally responsible for close-range clearing or use legal recon tools where available. Do not assume obscured space is empty.

sections.heading: Save utility when appropriate
paragraphs: A smoke needed for a later plant or rotation may be more valuable than an early cosmetic-looking placement. Consider the round's economy and current team position. Avoid automatically copying a full set of lineups regardless of the real defense.

sections.heading: Adjust to enemy habits
paragraphs: If defenders repeatedly push through a smoke, plan to hold its near edge or change timing. Do not treat the ability as an unbreakable barrier. Opponents can reposition and exploit predictable patterns.

sections.heading: Use the map and patch you have
paragraphs: Agents and maps evolve with updates. Verify current durations and placements in the live game or practice mode. Do not publish exact numerical effects based on outdated clips as permanent facts.

sections.heading: Evaluate teammate follow-through
paragraphs: After a round, ask whether the smoke enabled movement and whether allies understood its timing. Placement quality is measured by a useful action, not merely whether a screenshot shows a beautiful cloud.

sections.heading: How to test and adapt the method
paragraphs: Run a short controlled trial rather than changing several variables in one match. Start with the present game's supported interface and verify the map, agent, rules and team situation before applying a method. If something unexpected happens, communicate the observed fact, adapt and keep a useful fallback. After a few rounds, review the first decision that caused a problem. The best improvement is a repeatable action that teammates understand, not a lucky highlight, exaggerated win-rate claim or unauthorized utility script.
